mission: After the short clash fails to give Vara control, she takes Iressa hostage and pressures her memory. Ben sees a Jacen-shaped coercive option and refuses it. Iressa finishes corrupting the enemy’s copy and transmits her dying package to Ben and Talon — two things at once. First, the documentary chain Ben would need to bring Saba to make an institutional case. Second, the strategic revelation: she has figured out why the Vigil wants Jacen’s unfinished holocron specifically. The work on Recognition and Holding is not just dangerous knowledge — the Vigil intends to use it (with Aevyn’s help, as Jacen’s surviving student) for identity-level influence on high-value targets. She names the category of threat, not specific names. She dies denying Vara the clean version. Her fear should come out as herself: practical irritation, file anger, or one last debt/fee joke rather than sentimental martyrdom.
why_now: Vara has Iressa at knifepoint and is pressing her memory for what she sent. Ben sees a Jacen-shaped option — mind pressure and command, precise and coercive — that Jacen once taught him and that might extract enough control to get Iressa free. The moment of refusing it, while Iressa is still transmitting, is the scene’s load-bearing choice. She dies before Vara gets the clean version.
conflict: Ben sees the coercive option clearly — it is not abstract; it is a specific technique Jacen demonstrated. He refuses it because it would violate Iressa’s mind. Iressa finishes her work anyway, transmitting both the documentary chain and the strategic revelation about the holocron’s purpose. She dies active, not passive. Ben’s restraint preserved his line and cost a life.
turning_point: Ben and Talon escape with the clue and the revelation, but Iressa is dead.
closing_hook: Ben and Talon escape with the clue and the revelation, but Iressa is dead.
setting: Coruscant, same GAG quarantine archive — Vara holds Iressa hostage in the server-room aisle. Emergency lights pulse red. Iressa is bleeding from the ribs. Ben sees the Jacen-shaped coercive option and refuses it. Iressa transmits her dying package before Vara kills her.
emotional_trajectory: Iressa dies with agency. Ben’s guilt matters, but she is not reduced to a lesson for him. The reader must clearly understand that Ben saw another possible way, that it might have worked, and that it would have violated a mind. The transmission Iressa sends carries the strategic stakes forward — from this point on, Ben and the reader know what is really at stake on Iresh. Reader-onboarding / clarity note: Keep the Force ethics simple: Ben can use pressure and command in a way Jacen once taught, but refuses to cross that line. The death proves restraint can cost lives. Iressa’s short arc is clear: old Iressa buried discrepancies; new Iressa preserves one. Plain-language consequence of the revelation: this isn’t a completed Sith weapon. It’s Jacen’s notebook on how to shape people from the inside, and the Vigil wants to finish the work using the only student who could.

stakes.personal: Ben sees the Jacen-shaped coercive option with the clarity of someone who was taught it by demonstration. The wound is not that the option exists — it’s that he knows exactly how to use it. Refusing costs him certainty about the outcome. This is the scene that proves his restraint is a choice, not a limitation.
stakes.interpersonal: Iressa’s fear comes out as file anger and one last fee/debt joke rather than a plea. She is still herself while Vara presses her. The moment her transmission completes is the moment she has finished the job she owed — old Iressa buried discrepancies, new Iressa preserved one. Her arc closes as action, not martyrdom.
stakes.external: Iressa’s dying transmission carries two things: the documentary chain (the case Ben could bring to Saba) and the strategic revelation — Jacen’s unfinished holocron systematizes Recognition and Holding for identity-level influence on high-value targets. Iressa recovered a fragment of Jacen’s own sealed annotation naming the cache’s purpose by reconstructing around his encryption. She didn’t infer it; she found his own words. The Vigil intends to use Aevyn, as Jacen’s surviving student, to finish the work.

sensory_details: Emergency lights pulse red; the cabinet aisle smells of scorched plastoid from the quarantine-seal charges Greyline triggered at the exits. Iressa's breath is audible — quick, controlled, furious — in the silence between Vara's words. The transmission chip in her hand makes no sound while it sends. Ben notices the precise angle of Vara's blade and the specific pressure she's applying — not enough to kill yet, enough to make the mind start choosing.
canon_elements_needed: Shedu Maad / Hapes Jedi HQ continuity

turning_point_detail.trigger: Iressa's transmission completes — she sent everything she had. Vara, reading that her chance for a clean extraction is gone, acts.
turning_point_detail.shift: Iressa dies having preserved the clue. Vara gets nothing usable. Ben has the documentary chain and the revelation about Recognition, Holding, and the Vigil's intent — but he got them at the price of watching what refusal costs.
turning_point_detail.cost: Ben now knows that Jacen's notebook on how to shape people from the inside is the target, that Aevyn is the only one who can complete it, and that Iressa's specific annotation recovery means she found Jacen's own words naming the cache's purpose. That knowledge has a weight. He carries it out.

emotional_arc.start: Ben is in operational mode — holding the threat line, watching Vara press Iressa, calculating the coercive option without yet deciding.
emotional_arc.shift: He refuses the Jacen-shaped coercive option. The refusal is clean in his own mind and genuinely costs something: he watches the outcome of not acting unfold.
emotional_arc.end: Iressa is dead. She finished the job. Ben and Talon have the clue. Ben's guilt matters, but Iressa is not reduced to a lesson — she acted and she completed the act. Ben carries the weight of what he refused and what it cost.

key_beats.beat_description: Vara takes Iressa at knifepoint and presses her memory — demanding what was transmitted and to whom.
key_beats.state_change: Iressa's working time collapses to seconds; the question of whether Ben acts becomes the operative tension in the room.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The calculation running without permission: angle, duration, the specific technique and what it would cost Iressa's mind.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben sees the Jacen-shaped coercive option — specific, taught by demonstration — and refuses to use it.
key_beats.state_change: The refusal is clean in Ben's own reckoning and costs him certainty about the outcome: he watches what not-acting produces.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The hands staying where they are — not pulled back, just not moving — and the wait that follows.

key_beats.beat_description: Iressa finishes corrupting the enemy's copy and transmits her dying package — the documentary chain and the strategic revelation about the holocron — to Ben and Talon.
key_beats.state_change: The proof is transmitted; Vara gets nothing usable; the tactical situation resolves against Vara even as Iressa's position becomes fatal.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The reading of what is happening one beat too late to change it — the thing already done before the doing is fully registered.

key_beats.beat_description: Iressa's transmission carries Jacen's own sealed annotation naming Recognition and Holding as a systematic tool for identity-level influence on high-value targets — found, not inferred.
key_beats.state_change: The threat becomes concrete: this is not completed knowledge but Jacen's framework, and Aevyn is the only person positioned to finish it.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The weight of the specific words settling — not shock, the kind of recognition that makes the stomach go quiet.

key_beats.beat_description: Iressa dies with file anger and one last debt joke rather than a plea; Ben and Talon escape with the clue.
key_beats.state_change: Iressa's arc closes as action — old Iressa buried discrepancies, new Iressa preserved one — and Ben carries both the proof and the cost of refusal out of the archive.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Moving because stopping would mean accounting for it — the guilt deferred into forward motion.
